Graduate School Admission at UAF
Ready to start your graduate degree? Take the next step toward your academic goals
and research career today.
Launch UAF Application
Reach out to us.
Contact your UAF graduate program's department directly to learn more about specific
application requirements. Each program is unique — some require the GRE, while others
do not. Many programs also offer teaching and research assistantships that waive tuition
costs.
Browse Specific Program Requirements
Graduate Admission Requirements in Detail
General Requirements
In general, applicants may be admitted to a graduate program if they hold a bachelor's
degree from an accredited institution with at least a 3.0 (B) cumulative undergraduate
GPA and a 3.0 (B) GPA in their major field.
Standard Required Materials:
Resume or Curriculum Vitae
Statement of Academic and Professional Goals
Three official letters of recommendation
GRE or GMAT scores (as required by program)
$75 nonrefundable application fee
Note: Your program may require additional materials such as licenses, writing samples,
or a preliminary research prospectus.
Check Catalog for Full Requirements
Transcripts & Evaluation
Official Transcripts: Required from all post-secondary institutions attended. Transcripts must be delivered
directly in sealed institution envelopes or submitted electronically via a secure
transcript service (e.g., Parchment, National Student Clearinghouse).
In-Progress Coursework: Unofficial in-progress transcripts may be submitted for initial review, but final
official transcripts are required upon admission.
International Applicants: Must submit official academic records to The Evaluation Company (TEC) or World Education Services (WES) for a course-by-course credential evaluation. (Canadian institutions outside Quebec
are exempt). Official TOEFL or IELTS scores are also required.
Questions? Contact uaf-grad-admissions@alaska.edu.
Standardized Test Scores
Certain departments require GRE or GMAT scores, while others waive standardized test
requirements for applicants maintaining a 3.0+ GPA.
UAF GRE Institution Code: 4866
Are you an international student?
UAF international graduate students conduct impactful research across climate science,
oceanography, space physics, and more. Explore our international admissions portal
for guidance on visa acquisition, transcript evaluation, and campus resources.
International Admissions Guide
Financial Aid Essentials for Graduate Students
When planning your graduate degree financing, consider key factors that may affect
your aid eligibility:
Employment Status: Full-time work, part-time work, or assistantships.
Dependency Status: Dependents relying on your primary household income.
Residency & Taxes: State residency requirements and account balances.
Funding Opportunities: Assistantships offered directly through academic departments.
